newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook-Fuel oil soft, diesel firmer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook-Fuel oil soft, diesel firmer.

text.p: Asian fuel oil is expected to maintain its soft tone this week while gas oil might emerge from its recent sluggishness, traders said on Monday.
High sulphur fuel oil prices edged down last week over concerns that a Singapore trader which has been consistently purchasing cargoes since late June, might have covered its requirements.
The trader said it had been buying to meet its term contracts but it had not bid at high levels.
"His demand may still be there, but supplies are ample and there is no additional buying support. There is little room for prices to go up," one trader said.
Traders said the $100-per-tonne level, a previous support for the 180-cst grade fuel oil, has turned into a resistance level this week.
On the demand side, Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) will close a tender on Tuesday to buy 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for September delivery.
The tender is seeking a 38,000-tonne low-pour cargo for September 1-15 and a high-pour cargo for September 11-30.
In the gas oil market, traders said physical fundamentals have not changed with little Chinese demand as authorities were bent on both snuffing out smuggling and severely curbing legal imports.

However, the market was being propped up by speculation in the swaps market led by a major and western traders last week. They said players were trading on the East-West spread -- buying the east and selling the west -- to position themselves for possible cargo movements westward. So far, three cargoes have been fixed for South America.
With China's continued absence, the market is looking towards India to provide some support.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a tender, closing July 31, to buy 0.5 and 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil for deliveries in September.
Traders said prompt gas oil values might have almost reached their bottom at the current $19.80-$20.00 range, with the support placed at $19.50, a three-year low.
Jet fuel is seen to remain steady as a Singapore trader was said to be pricing its July cargoes into Indonesia.

But traders said the fundamentals on jet are even worse than gas oil and they considered the current jet/gas oil spread at over $2.00 per barrel to be too wide and that it should be limited to around $1.00.
Light distillate stocks figures from Singapore's trade development board showed a build in the week ending July 16, of over 1.8 million to 8.016 million barrels, the highest since April 1994.
Traders mainly attributed the build to gasoline as the Asian market remains depresses amid thin buying interest.

Naphtha fundamentals in comparison, were healthy with Singapore barrels attracting premiums of as much as $1.00 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes. In the first half of the year, premiums hovered below the 50-cent mark.
